prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project with billing
prerequisites.detail: The marketplace guide lists enabling billing in a Cloud project as a prerequisite. Use an Owner or Editor account.

prerequisites.title: Published branding status
prerequisites.detail: You must have a published branding status before requesting data access verification.

steps.title: Create Cloud project and OAuth client
steps.detail: Sign in with an Owner or Editor account, create the project and OAuth client, and enable the Gmail API.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Pick the least-powerful scopes that work, and draft written justifications for each.
steps.done_when: Scope list and justifications are ready.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config with your client ID and secret via Composio's API. Add the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard to the Google OAuth client.

steps.title: Publish branding and submit for brand verification
steps.detail: Complete the consent screen and submit.

steps.title: Record demo video
steps.detail: Record the flow showing how each requested scope is used.

steps.title: Submit scope verification justifications
steps.detail: Enter justifications in the Verification required dialog and click Submit.
steps.done_when: Status shows in the OAuth Verification Center.

steps.title: Wait for Google verification
steps.detail: Answer Google's clarification questions promptly, since resubmission delays review.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Restricted scopes may require a security assessment, repeated every 12 months.
steps.done_when: You hold a Letter of Validation.

traps.title: Restricted scopes add months
traps.detail: The security assessment is the longest step, and it must be repeated every 12 months in full even if the app did not change.

traps.title: Testing mode caps at 100 users
traps.detail: Apps in Testing status allow only users on the test list, up to 100. Only basic identity scopes are exempt.

traps.title: Verified does not beat admin settings
traps.detail: A Workspace admin can still block your app, even if it is verified.

traps.title: New scopes mean new verification
traps.detail: Plan verification time into any feature that needs a new scope.

blockers.symptom: 'This app isn't verified' warning on the consent screen
blockers.what_it_means: Your app requests sensitive scopes and has not been verified.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit for verification. Users can continue past it with Advanced during development.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft scope justifications and a demo script.

blockers.symptom: Customer's Workspace users cannot install or authorize the app
blockers.what_it_means: The admin restricts high-risk Gmail scopes to trusted apps, or blocks unverified ones.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to allowlist your OAuth client ID.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft admin instructions with your client ID.

evidence.answer: Yes, apps using restricted Gmail scopes must repeat the CASA security assessment every 12 months, counted from the effective date of the previous Letter of Validation.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: We require the annual CASA security reassessment to be a comprehensive test of your app, regardless of any changes made to the app.
evidence.answer: The annual reassessment is a comprehensive test required regardless of whether the app changed.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If your application has fewer than 100 users, you will not need to undergo app verification until that threshold is hit.
evidence.answer: Per a Nylas blog (dated 2019, updated 2021, so possibly outdated), apps with fewer than 100 users need not undergo verification until they reach 100 users; other exemptions also listed (testing, internal-only Workspace use).

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: When adding new sensitive scopes , you simply need to undergo app re-verification, complete all the steps for your new scope and re-submit for verification at no cost. This typically takes 2-4 weeks
evidence.answer: Per Nylas (2019/2021 post, dated), re-verification for new sensitive scopes typically takes 2-4 weeks and is free.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: This verification process can take just a few days or as long as several weeks end-to-end.
evidence.answer: Nylas reports standard OAuth verification takes a few days to several weeks end-to-end (older 2019/2021 source).

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The process can take anywhere from a few weeks to (more commonly) multiple months, depending on the complexity of the application.
evidence.answer: Nylas reports the restricted-scope security assessment more commonly takes multiple months; remediation retests lengthen it further.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: If Google has clarification questions based on your original submission, you'll need to address those questions and resubmit your app, which could delay the review process.
evidence.answer: A common blocker is Google's clarification questions on the original submission, which require resubmission and delay review.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: The honest range Google quotes is four to six weeks of back-and-forth (initial scan, fix the findings, rescan, sign off).
evidence.answer: A developer's report of Gmail/Google CASA Tier 2 review: Google quotes four to six weeks of back-and-forth; the developer was given a deadline (Aug 3, 2026) and was verified June 29, 2026.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If an app is only used by users within your own organization, then these additional requirements do not apply.
evidence.answer: Restricted-scope additional requirements (verification, CASA) do not apply to apps used only by users within the developer's own organization; this is an exemption, not a user-count threshold.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote:
We prohibit third parties from selling user data or using
user data for advertising purposes.
evidence.answer: Google Workspace user data policy prohibits third parties from selling user data or using it for advertising, and the Gmail scopes are not allowed for certain use cases such as spam or unsolicited commercial mail.
